body.heading: Start with the concrete
paragraphs: Vague prompts like 'write about your feelings' can stall anyone. Concrete ones work better: 'Describe the room you are in as if for someone who will never see it.' 'What sound did you hear first this morning?'
Specific questions give your memory something to grab. Answer in plain sentences and do not worry about whether it sounds like proper journaling.

body.heading: A handful to rotate
paragraphs: Try these on different days: What is one thing I know now that I did not know last month? What would I do this week if I knew it would work out? What am I tired of, and what is one honest sentence about it?
Keep a short list inside your notebook's cover. On a blank day, pick one at random, set a timer for ten minutes, and write without lifting the pen more than you need to.

takeaway: Concrete prompts, ten minutes, no audience: that is enough to begin.
